glossary.note: 钢铁雄心4 术语对照表。翻译时严格遵守，保证全站译名一致。

style.register: 游戏指南体，简体中文，简洁直陈，不用敬语，不用『您』。
style.numbers: 数字、百分比、游戏内数值原样保留（如 10%、+5%）。
style.placeholders: ⟦0⟧ ⟦1⟧ 等占位符必须原样保留且不得增删、不得调换顺序；它们代表图标或链接。
style.markup: 不要输出 HTML 标签；保留原文的换行与项目符号结构。
style.properNouns: 国家、人物、舰名等专有名词使用通用中文译名（如 German Reich → 德意志国，Adolf Hitler → 阿道夫·希特勒）；Paradox 未汉化的专有名词可保留英文并加中文注释。
style.consistency: 同一英文术语在全站必须使用同一译名。

instructions: Translate every "en" string into Simplified Chinese (zh-Hans), game-guide register. Follow glossary.json strictly. Keep ⟦0⟧-style placeholders, numbers, units and wiki markup exactly. Return only {"items":[{"k":"...","zh":"..."}]} with the same k values.

units.en: ⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧: In multiplayer, the practice of deliberately performing actions that provide additional civilian factories to a specific, allied country, such as ⟦2⟧ resources even when they are not needed, purchasing unnecessary ⟦3⟧, or deliberately buying useless equipment from them through the ⟦4⟧.

⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧: A strategy or part of a strategy that provides some notable advantage and that is unlikely to be intentional by the game's developers. Somewhat related to exploits, but usually considered "softer" and more fair to use. Examples include constant conversion, completely removing an enemy's planning bonus by having every member of a ⟦2⟧ set one of their spies to build a network near their frontline, tying down an enemy's navy by using many tiny ⟦3⟧ task forces to Always Engage, et al.
⟦0⟧: to make a country succeed far beyond expectations. (A takeoff on the polandball meme.)
⟦0⟧: One's rightful land. Also a takeoff from polandball.
⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧: Being able to quickly defeat all enemy forces in a province without any effort besides right-clicking the province to order selected units to move onto it.

⟦0⟧: Dedicated player who focuses their attention on producing, micromanaging, and maximizing bonuses for ⟦1⟧, preferably the super-heavy variety. Somewhat common in multiplayer games, usually done by minor powers whose land unit bonuses are eclipsed by their teammates', e.g., ⟦2⟧ for the Axis and ⟦3⟧ for the Allies.

⟦0⟧: A cheesy strategy where the high ⟦1⟧ costs of expensive tanks and aircraft are bypassed by simultaneously producing basic, bare-bones designs that are marked as outdated and ⟦2⟧ them immediately to their final designs. This can happen because the ⟦3⟧ costs of these equipments is often incurred only by the base chassis/airframe and the main armament, while these are only a minority of the total production costs of the final design. Especially with the help of ⟦4⟧, the amount of production lost to this strategy ends up being negligible, while the ⟦5⟧ savings from not having to ⟦6⟧ for as many resources can be huge.

⟦0⟧: Historically, the day of the Allied naval landings in occupied France in Operation Overlord; used to describe any in-game naval invasion of continental Europe from Britain, sometimes as a verb (as in "The Allies are D-Daying!").
⟦0⟧: Division(s), the basic combat unit on the map.
⟦0⟧: An extremely large enemy force in a single province; seldom used on land in HoI4, but often for navies.

⟦0⟧: Attacking the same enemy province from two different provinces in a way where the attacks are treated as two separate combats instead of a singular one, done by queueing up moves for the divisions in two different provinces in a specific way. This ensures that enemy units get the "in multiple combats" penalty in both combats, which would normally only be applied if they were both attacking and defending at the same time.
⟦0⟧: Abbreviation for El Alamein, the site of a few famous historical battles in World War 2 and a notorious choke point for land armies in Egypt.

⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧: The practice of rapidly switching ⟦2⟧, usually bombers, between multiple air zones, either to abuse the mechanics behind naval strike and port strike air missions to make attacks happen far more frequently than intended, or simply to overload the micromanagement abilities of enemy air controllers in multiplayer.
⟦0⟧: Abbreviation for Gibraltar, a notable choke point controlling access between the Mediterranean Sea and the larger Atlantic Ocean.
⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧: Bastardization of the very annoying ⟦2⟧ combat tactic, usually when unlocked through the Mass Mobilization branch of the ⟦3⟧ land doctrine.

⟦0⟧: Deliberately keeping units in battles without capturing provinces to generate XP. Often used in early wars before World War 2 with volunteer divisions to help level up ⟦1⟧ to high levels with good skills and traits, rarely also used with ⟦2⟧ (and more difficult to do with them) for similar reasons. Pre-grinds: Done in many multiplayer-oriented mods and custom save games to avoid people wanting to grind generals manually and therefore speed up the game, as grinding an normally be somewhat micro-intensive.
⟦0⟧: Done in many multiplayer-oriented mods and custom save games to avoid people wanting to grind ⟦1⟧ manually and therefore speed up the game, as grinding an normally be somewhat micro-intensive.

⟦0⟧: Abbreviation for infantry equipment, the most important ⟦1⟧ in terms of providing a battalion's combat stats for all infantry and mobile battalions. Usually followed by a number to indicate its year: gun 0 is 1918 infantry equipment, gun 1 is 1936 infantry equipment, gun 2 is 1939 infantry equipment, and gun 3 is 1942 infantry equipment.

⟦0⟧: In multiplayer, a reference to players who actively pay attention to a delicate in-game situation and actively respond to it (or used in insults for players who cannot or do not do this when expected of them), usually in the form of micro.

⟦0⟧: Deliberately letting an event expire or waiting until right before it does to select an option in it. Because a lot of events only apply their effects after a country has clicked an option in it, holding events like this can delay undesirable effects (e.g., the Allies handing the Sudetenland over to Germany) for a few weeks that can end up being crucial.
⟦0⟧: Abbreviation for howitzer tanks, i.e., tank designs that use howitzers for their main armament, giving them a lot of soft attack but very little hard attack.

⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧: The practice of leaving a research slot deliberately empty for a month before spending the accrued research progress to help complete a specific, high-priority tech faster. This is done by researching said "juggled" tech with one slot while leaving another empty, and when the empty slot has accrued enough research progress, switching the first slot to research a different technology and then continuing to research the "juggled" tech with the slot that was left empty.
⟦0⟧: The political action of building a propaganda case against a country to justify a declaration of war.

⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧: In multiplayer, spending a lot of time in the game's lobby waiting for the game to start, waiting for players whose game crashed or who went out-of-sync to reconnect to the game, and/or waiting for hot-joins to finish loading in.
⟦0⟧: Slang for numerical ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, and other points.
⟦0⟧: A marine division with a few mechanized battalions included, usually to greatly increase the division's HP and therefore make it last longer when performing ⟦1⟧ using the Force Attack ⟦2⟧.

⟦0⟧: Considered the opposite of "micro", refers to the larger choices made and strategy used outside of controlling individual units, including for ⟦1⟧, ⟦2⟧, ⟦3⟧, ⟦4⟧ expenses, and the order and timing of ⟦5⟧.

⟦0⟧: Short for "micromanagement", refers to controlling individual units, as well as the attention and the skill required to do it well under time pressure. Pause-Micro: In multiplayer, queueing up orders for many individual units while a game is paused, taking advantage of there being no time pressure present to do so. Last Stand Micro or Force Attack Micro: The practice of setting of a dummy order-of-battle with lower-quality generals that can then be used to dramatically reduce the command power cost of performing the respectively named commander abilities. This is done by temporarily assigning the specific divisions for which the ability is to be used to one of those dummy generals, activating the commander ability on the dummy general, and only assigning the unit(s) back to their regular generals after the ability is no longer needed.
⟦0⟧: In multiplayer, queueing up orders for many individual units while a game is paused, taking advantage of there being no time pressure present to do so.

⟦0⟧ or ⟦1⟧: The practice of setting of a dummy order-of-battle with lower-quality ⟦2⟧ that can then be used to dramatically reduce the ⟦3⟧ cost of performing the respectively named ⟦4⟧. This is done by temporarily assigning the specific divisions for which the ability is to be used to one of those dummy ⟦5⟧, activating the commander ability on the dummy general, and only assigning the unit(s) back to their regular ⟦6⟧ after the ability is no longer needed.
⟦0⟧: A software package that modifies the game, written by the player community. Compare with DLC.
⟦0⟧: In multiplayer, a player playing co-operatively on a larger nation who is meant to focus on nothing else besides micromanaging that country's navy.
⟦0⟧: A strategy where a country puts far more emphasis on building up a (surface) navy than is deemed sensible for that country.
⟦0⟧: Nuclear bombs, or the act of using them.
⟦0⟧: Organization, required for any division to continue or engage combat. Deorg: A division running out of organization, forcing it to break off an attack or retreat when defending.
⟦0⟧: A division running out of organization, forcing it to break off an attack or retreat when defending.
⟦0⟧: After having ⟦1⟧ an enemy country's cipher, revealing it for a major temporary bonus at the cost of needing to re-decrypt their cipher after the bonus expires.
⟦0⟧: Abbreviation for a ⟦1⟧ who increases the country's ⟦2⟧ gain, usually one with the Silent Workhorse trait.

⟦0⟧: Reinforcements in manpower, equipment or both. Reinforce meme: Defeating all divisions currently in combat before reserve divisions in the same province can enter combat, forcing them to retreat without fighting (or causing them to be destroyed if encircled).
⟦0⟧: Defeating all divisions currently in combat before ⟦1⟧ divisions in the same province can enter combat, forcing them to retreat without fighting (or causing them to be destroyed if encircled).

⟦0⟧: In multiplayer, having the game's host save the game, exit the game (thereby disconnecting all other players), then host a new game from the save taken. Often used as an attempted fix for when several players keep crashing and/or going out-of-sync to the point that the game cannot actually be played.
⟦0⟧: When the Axis captures Egypt and advances south into Africa.

⟦0⟧: Reloading earlier saves when something goes wrong in order to set things right. Often considered a negative trait. Ironman mode prevents savescumming, unless circumvented through manual file copying.

⟦0⟧: In multiplayer, the act of exploiting a certain bug around ⟦1⟧ that allow them to be launched against a player without triggering the visual or audio alert for them for an ongoing naval invasion.

⟦0⟧: Sending a single division or small group of divisions to race ahead through a breakthrough and capture tiles, VPs, or ports without securing the tiles behind them, in order to disrupt industry or enemy supply, or VP snipe an enemy country and cause it to capitulate. Often results in the division(s) used being encircled and lost.

⟦0⟧: A division with a single armored battalion, usually a heavy tank destroyer or heavy tank, that otherwise has no other armored battalions. This is meant to provide a lot of armor and/or piercing to the division for little cost by taking advantage of the way armor and piercing are calculated for divisions. Considered overpowered by a lot of people in early versions of the game, they tend to be far less cost-effective in current versions of the game.
⟦0⟧: Abbreviation for a ⟦1⟧ who increases the country's ⟦2⟧, usually one with the Popular Figurehead trait.
⟦0⟧: Strategic bomber or strategic redeploy or strategy.

⟦0⟧: In multiplayer, the practice of one country buying the ⟦1⟧ of an ally to offset said ally using their civilian factories to purchase the first country's resources, even when those resources would go unused. Also often used to offset the ⟦2⟧ cost of obtaining ⟦3⟧.

⟦0⟧: Using paratroopers, snaking fast divisions, and/or naval invasions to capture the victory point tiles of an enemy country and thus cause it to capitulate, bypassing most of its army. When unsuccessful, likely to result in the divisions used being encircled and lost.
⟦0⟧: The act of declaring war / being declared war upon.
⟦0⟧: The cheapest, most basic heavy cruiser that can be made whose sole purpose is to be designated a ⟦1⟧ to give its country extra war support.
Abbreviations sometimes used for countries. Often written in all caps despite not being initialisms, many of those are originating from the country tags used by Paradox.

⟦0⟧ (⟦1⟧) are threads posted to the HOI4 forums or a personal web site or blog written by players about their ongoing games. They can be written from the game player's personal point of view, or can be written from a fictitious narrative perspective, like a serialized novel. Some writers also blend the two elements, going from a metagame discussion to a fictitious narrative set in their game's alternate history world.

"I had a rough time as Austria this last session. It started when Ulm, that darned ⟦0⟧, suddenly brought in half the HRE against me when I declared war on it. In all my playthroughs, this was the first time I ever was faced with such a nasty coalition. Before I knew it, not only was I facing the coalition, but the Ottoman Empire decided to make a DOW on me while I was in the thick of it!“
"Let me tell you a story, a story about how a small and obscure nation, would come and rise to glory and ultimately shape history forever...
